title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 69
paragraphs: The victors, then, were pressing after Xerxes's troops, pursuing and slaughtering them. During this panic, news was brought to the other Greeks — those who had taken position around the temple of Hera and had been absent from the battle — that a battle had taken place and Pausanias's troops were winning. On hearing this, without forming any order, the Corinthians and those near them turned to go along the skirts of the mountain and the low hills on the way leading straight up to the temple of Demeter, while the Megarians, Phliasians, and those near them went by the plain along the smoothest route. But when the Megarians and Phliasians drew near the enemy, the Theban cavalry caught sight of them from a distance hurrying along in no order, and rode up to attack — their cavalry commander being Asopodoros son of Timander. Falling upon them, they killed six hundred, and pursued and drove the rest to Kithairon.
